entries.notes: Use Rev. 3 vocabulary in the D39 containment, eradication and recovery plan and the D40 incident summary. plan_fact_checks.claim: Plan section 4 and section 16 item 7: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 is final (April 2025) and frames incident response as part of CSF 2.0 risk management.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/final and csrc.nist.gov/news/2025/nist-revises-sp-800-61 in search results: title 'Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management: A CSF 2.0 Community Profile', published April 2025 (finalized 2025-04-03), supersedes Rev. 2 (2012), which NIST withdrew the same day. The project page says the document no longer holds detailed procedures and focuses on risk management across CSF 2.0 functions: Govern, Identify and Protect as preparation, Detect, Respond and Recover as incident response proper. The initial public draft was 2024-04-03.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Plan section 7.2 W08-Q08 and section 8: SP 800-61r3 frames incident response within broader cybersecurity risk management.

gaps: The shared web-search budget of the authoring run (200 calls per turn) ran out before a last attempt to read TryHackMe's free-training blog posts for per-room free flags, so every TryHackMe entry stays UNKNOWN on access.

No Hack The Box Sherlock page was found at its canonical address (app.hackthebox.com/sherlocks/<name>) in any search result, and no search result showed that a Sherlock is retired. The blog also names Meerkat, Bumblebee, Litter and Tracer as beginner DFIR Sherlocks; they were not registered. A retired Sherlock needs VIP+, so the hosted free alternatives are the LetsDefend and CyberDefenders items.

No official Microsoft or vendor page was found for Prefetch, Amcache, ShimCache or the registry hive file list (the Microsoft 'Registry hives' page was not returned). Artifact semantics rest on the Eric Zimmerman site, TryHackMe room text and CyberDefenders lab text; the SANS Windows forensic analysis poster was not searched. Statements about what Prefetch, Amcache or LNK files prove should be labelled INFERRED or ASSUMED.

journalctl: whether bare --since and --until values are local time or UTC, journal retention and rotation, and wtmp, btmp and lastlog rotation were not confirmed in search results; the man pages utmp(5), last(1), lastlog(8), ausearch(8) and audit.rules(7) were returned but are not registered. The week 8 expansion asks for Linux journaling and log-rotation caveats, so the author must source or label them.

No Linux memory forensics resource was registered. Volatility 3 needs a hand-built symbol table for Linux (README), so a Linux memory exercise needs preparation. LetsDefend 'Linux Memory Forensics' (app.letsdefend.io/challenge/linux-memory-forensics) and TryHackMe 'Profiles' were returned but not registered.

The TryHackMe Velociraptor room (tryhackme.com/room/velociraptorhp) was returned and reported as Premium or Max only, so it was left out; the Velociraptor documentation is the only registered Velociraptor resource. The only tier statements found were Incident Handling Process as Tier I (path page, layout may misalign) and Rhadamanthys as a premium CyberDefenders lab (not registered).

Autopsy (sleuthkit.org/autopsy/docs/user-docs/4.22.0/quick_start_guide.html), the NIST CSF 2.0 white paper (nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/CSWP/NIST.CSWP.29.pdf), the HTB article 'A (realistic) template for writing incident response reports' (hackthebox.com/blog/writing-incident-response-report-template) and the Microsoft 1102 and Get-WinEvent pages (week 7 holds Get-WinEvent as w07-ms-get-winevent) were returned by search but not registered to stay within the entry limit; an author may add them under the same rules.
